reading: Greenidge Generation Holdings is a publicly traded company listed on NASDAQ under ticker GREE that operates a bitcoin mining data center co-located with its own natural gas power plant in Dresden, New York, in the Finger Lakes region on Seneca Lake. Atlas Holdings, a private equity firm, acquired the power plant in 2014 and converted it from coal to natural gas in 2016 before Greenidge repurposed the site to power onsite bitcoin mining, becoming one of the first vertically integrated power-plant-to-bitcoin-mining businesses to go public. The facility has been a focal point of New York State's debate over cryptocurrency mining and climate policy, with the state Department of Environmental Conservation denying an air permit renewal in 2022 on the grounds that the plant's greenhouse gas emissions conflicted with New York's climate goals, a decision Greenidge contested. A November 2024 court ruling rejected a state effort to shut the mining operation down over climate concerns, though the underlying regulatory dispute has continued. Greenidge's business model, self-mining bitcoin using power generated at a company-owned plant rather than leasing data center capacity to outside tenants, distinguishes it sharply from the colocation and wholesale operators that dominate this registry, placing it instead alongside other power-first crypto mining operators like Atlas Power and Marathon Digital Holdings.
